references.text: The same expression 'לַחְשֹׁב מַחֲשָׁבֹת' (to devise skillful works) is used concerning Bezalel when his skills are described again.
The preceding verse states that God filled Bezalel with His Spirit, wisdom, and understanding to carry out this work.
The materials gold, silver, and bronze are first mentioned here as gifts the Israelites were to give for the tabernacle.
It repeats that God filled the craftsmen with wisdom to perform all kinds of artistic works.
The fulfillment of God's call to Bezalel and Oholiab, who begin the artistic work with gold, silver, and bronze.
Hiram from Tyre was filled with wisdom and understanding to work in bronze for Solomon's temple, similar to Bezalel's calling.
Solomon requests a craftsman skilled in gold, silver, and bronze for the temple construction, reminiscent of Bezalel's skills.
A clear thematic parallel between Bezalel and Hiram regarding the ability to devise and execute skillful works for God's house.
Connects Solomon's need for a skilled man with Bezalel's profile of divine devising and craftsmanship.
